title: auth: standardize auth header semantics + scoped tokens, nonce header, CORS, and OpenAI-compat updates
author: Evelyn Zhang
description: Motivation: We have accumulated several ad-hoc auth behaviors across the OpenAI-compat layer and internal API gateway (project vs org keys, scoped tokens, CORS preflight handling, and a request-signing nonce header). This PR consolidates semantics and makes the compatibility surface deterministic so downstream SDKs and proxies can rely on a single documented contract. What this PR does: - Introduces a single canonical header precedence and semantics doc (implemented in api/compat/auth.rs + docs/openai_compat/auth.md). - Adds support for scoped tokens (token:scope pair encoded in the Authorization header) with explicit scope parsing and validation hooks (auth service + runtime checks). - Adds optional X-Redwood-Nonce header used by request signing flows; server validates nonce format and rejects replays for non-idempotent endpoints. Nonce support is off by default and gated by feature flag. - Tightens CORS semantics for browser SDKs: we now set Access-Control-Allow-Origin based on project-level allowed origins metadata and explicitly expose Authorization and X-Redwood-Nonce in Access-Control-Expose-Headers; preflight responds with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials when a project allows credentials. - Makes OpenAI-compat layer prefer: 1) Bearer tokens with project-scoped prefix (project:<id>:<token>), 2) Bearer tokens with org scope (org:<id>:<token>), 3) legacy API keys in X-Api-Key for backwards compatibility. The migration plan is documented in docs/openai_compat/auth.md. Checklist: - [x] Spec and docs added - docs/openai_compat/auth.md - [x] Runtime parsing and precedence implemented - api/compat/openai_auth.rs, auth/service.rs - [x] SDK TS changes for header handling - redwood-sdk-typescript/src/auth.ts - [x] End-to-end tests added for CORS preflight and nonce handling - tests/integration/auth_cors_nonce.test.ts - [x] Feature flag for nonce and scoped-token parsing - config/feature_flags.yaml Notes: This is API-surface only (no storage schema changes). Scoped tokens are validated against auth service introspection; this PR adds the parsing/metadata plumbing but defers advanced ACL policy changes to a follow-up (ENG-4257).
commits_summary: 4 commits: initial spec + docs, implement scoped token parsing and precedence, add nonce validation and feature flag, E2E tests and SDK compatibility fixes
code_changes_highlight: - api/compat/openai_auth.rs: added TokenType enum, parse_scoped_token(), header_precedence() helpers. - auth/service.rs: added introspect_scoped_token() and nonce validation hook behind feature flag. - pkg/http/cors.rs: updated preflight handling to consult project metadata and expose Authorization,X-Redwood-Nonce. - redwood-sdk-typescript/src/auth.ts: updated default header construction to support project:<id>:<token> style tokens and browser preflight guidance.

e2e_test_notes: Added auth_cors_nonce.test.ts covering: CORS preflight for credentialed requests, Access-Control-Expose-Headers contains Authorization and X-Redwood-Nonce, scoped token parsing with project and org prefixes, and nonce replay rejection for non-idempotent POSTs.
release_notes: - Stabilize OpenAI-compat auth header semantics: explicit precedence between project-scoped, org-scoped, and legacy X-Api-Key. - Add scoped token parsing and basic introspection plumbing (requires auth service). - Introduce optional X-Redwood-Nonce header for request signing flows (feature-flagged). - Tighten CORS preflight and exposed headers to support browser SDKs using Authorization and nonce headers.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Breaking clients that rely on implicit header precedence or old X-Api-Key-only behavior. Mitigation: backwards-compatible fallback to X-Api-Key, feature flag for nonce, and docs/migration guide. We will monitor auth_metrics and roll back the feature flag if rollout shows regressions.
